title: Current Unity campaign flow
status: Synced from desktop Unity source; map edits do not change game code
calendarRule: Four fixed councils in 1452: January strategic focus, April fortress warning, June Orban and December Union. February, March, May, July, August, September, October and November are selectable. January 1453 brings the Genoese and, provisionally, Hungry Mouths; February 1453 is selectable. March resolves the outpost castles, then Easter and the siege. Chain, commander and fleet orders are selectable preparations, not mandatory March events. Career options use persistent main-menu achievement counts earned across games.

events.title: A Fortress Rises on the Bosphorus

choices.label: Send a formal protest to the Sultan and the Christian courts. 1,000 gold; public morale +5; one diplomatic secret.

choices.text:
The agent returns among the suppliers with plans concealed in a ledger. One secret gained; the reconnaissance advantage is secured.
The agent is exposed and executed. No report reaches the City.

choices.label: Our answer will come from our own walls. No cost; troop morale +5.
choices.text: The garrison hears your defiance. The Ottoman work continues.

As your guards approach Orban, he screams and activates some sort of rigged grenade, triggering a massive explosion, which tears him and your soldiers into pieces. The whole throne room turns into an inferno and the blast wave throws you at the wall with the strength of a murderous giant. As you lie dying on the floor in a pool of your own blood, you think of what fate awaits your City…

The servants whisper among themselves that he consorts with the devils at night, for they can hear constant explosions coming from his workshop and he constantly smells of sulphur. choices.label: We shall support Orthodox Church unto death - send Cardinal Isidore and his heretical ideas somewhere far away. \[Isidore leaves permanently: unavailable as adviser or commander.\]
choices.text: Damned be those heretics, war or peace, we shall remain Orthodox. Your decision causes a brief celebration among your elites, but you know that your decision will reduce the likelihood that Catholic nations will aid us. Cardinal Isidore is exiled to convert heathens in Lapland, he is never heard from again. \[Noble Support +10\] \[Priest Support +15\] \[Religion - the Great Schism persists\]

choices.label: We must seek to Mend the Schism, adopt Catholicism fully!
choices.text: The time has come to swallow our pride and admit our fault. The Emperor will convert to Catholicism and require everyone in the palace to do the same. We will fully embrace Union of Florence - Roma suprema est. Your decision will cause anger among our priesthood and the nobles, but the Catholic nations will rejoice and we hope that the Pope shall call for a new crusade to save Constantinople. \[Noble Support -20\] \[Priest Support -30\] \[Religion - the Great Schism is mended\]

choices.label: The Emperor shall embrace Union of Florence, but will not enforce it. \[Isidore remains available as adviser and commander.\]

choices.label: Let us defend the City together before we settle the fate of Christendom. \[Retain Orthodoxy and Isidore; clergy support -5 points; no full-Union aid benefits.\] #focus:3
choices.text: You summon Orthodox and Latin representatives to swear a wartime compact. The Empire retains its Orthodox doctrine; Latin defenders may worship according to their rites. Isidore accepts your invitation to remain as an envoy and potential commander. Some clergy resent the accommodation, and the Pope receives no promise of submission. For now, you ask both churches to defend the same walls.

choices.label: We need every blade we can get, let us promise him the isle of Lemnos if he manages to help us defend our city!
choices.text: You promise Giustiniani the isle of Lemnos if the City survives. He accepts before the wine is poured. His men unload their arms and march to the walls. Your nobles mutter that the Empire is being sold piecemeal to mercenaries.

choices.label: Turn them away, Giustiniani is too ambitious, we cannot trust him!
choices.text: You make a decision that additional support from the Genoese is not worth the risk of them essentially taking over your City. Your decision strengthens your position among the nobility and priests, but Galatan podestà is not pleased...

choices.label: While Giustiniani will not be easy to control, we do need his troops... Poison him. #focus:4
choices.text: Lord Giovanni is greeted with a great feast. Unfortunately, over the following weeks he begins to feel increasingly sick, until he unfortunately dies. His men soon discover and kill a spy among his staff that was secretly putting poison into his food. Accursed Turks must have felt the danger from this noble man! His troops are now taken over by Francesco, his second-in-command, a skilled commander, but a commoner with much more manageable ambitions.

choices.label: The City is the final bastion of the Roman civilisation and everyone is welcome, open the gates!
choices.text: Thousands upon thousands of people flock through the gate of St.Romanus. You come to inspect the crowds yourself and thousands of cheering, happy faces greet you. Everyone, even the nobles, feels that this is the right thing to do. For the time being you feel that you are doing your duty as the saviour of your people. What effect it will have, only time will tell. \[Noble Support +5\] \[Priest Support +10\] \[Troop Morale +10\] \[Public Morale +30\] \[City Population is now {GetPopulation()} \]

choices.label: We need to save the flower of the nation, but leave the peasants beyond the gate. Tax those who enter - everyone needs to contribute to the defence!
choices.text: You open the gates to the nobles and their servants, priests, merchants, craftsmen and tax all of them on entry to help pay for the siege costs. Your decision is rational, but depressing. No one seriously objects, but there is a feeling of gloom around the city. Everyone is thinking - what if I had ended up on the other side of the gate? \[Noble Support -10\] \[Priest Support -10\] \[Troop Morale -10\] \[Public Morale -10\] \[City Population is now {GetPopulation()} \] \[Your treasury is now {GetInt("iMoney")} \]

choices.label: Close the gate, we are full. No one is to be admitted inside - we will be barely able to feed the population we already have.
choices.text: The wailing of the refugees beyond the gate doesn't let you sleep for a few days, but soon, they realise that nothing will change and start departing. You may have turned the hungry mouths away, but most of the City sees you as a cruel ruler who betrayed his own people. Only time will tell if you were right to do this. \[Noble Support -5\] \[Priest Support -15\] \[Troop Morale -15\] \[Public Morale -30\]

choices.label: [Focus - Mobilisation\] Allow everyone in, but press all the able bodied refugees to serve in our armed forces. Send the peasants to train with the spears and the hunters shall become archers. #focus:1
[Focus - Diplomacy and Spycraft\] Order our agents to divert as many refugees away from the city by spreading rumours. #focus:4

The plan works, our agents manage to successfully divert the majority of the refugees away from Constantinople by spreading rumours among the refugees about the awful conditions in the City, while mentioning that Peloponnese is very nice this time of year and not as far as it seems, so they should consider going there instead. \[Money -2500\]

choices.text: Your speech leaves a generally good impression on everyone gathered at the Hagia Sophia, but the nobles and the general population love it more than the rest.

choices.label: Soldiers of Christ! We have gathered here under the majestic dome of our blessed temple, to worship our God and to steel ourselves to defend our creed...
choices.text: Your speech leaves a generally good impression on everyone gathered at the Hagia Sophia, but the troops and the priests love it more than the rest.

choices.label: My faithful subjects, all who live and breathe to serve our great cause - it is time for us to prepare to meet our enemies...
choices.text: Your speech leaves a generally good impression on everyone gathered at the Hagia Sophia.

choices.label: [Focus - War Economy\] Order the Varangian Guard to close the doors and make everyone pay a war tax before they leave. Make exception for the priests if they help you convince the rest. #focus:2
choices.text: People feel somewhat betrayed, but there's little they can do and the priests are happy to preach to them about the joys of donating for the common cause. choices.label: It is not for the speeches that we have gathered here! Let everyone feast and enjoy themselves for one last time before the siege begins! Let us celebrate, for tomorrow we may die!
choices.text: On your orders, the guards roll in barrels of wine and start handing out bread, while musicians strike up uplifting tunes. The priests are unhappy about their temple becoming a feast hall, but they cannot do anything. People who moments ago were sullen and concerned, soon relax, drink and laugh. You can only hope that this last proper feast will help them withstand the coming months of trials and deprivation.

choices.label: Greet our guests - send the cavalry to harass their forward formations, but avoid serious engagements.
choices.text:
Your cavalry, adept at hit-and-run tactics, successfully disrupts the Ottoman vanguard, overrunning a surprised column of slaves, engineers and cooks and inflicting notable damage without being drawn into a decisive battle. One of your knights even manages to set a gunpowder wagon on fire, exploding it and destroying a few enemy cannons. The manoeuvre not only sets the stage for a more fortified defence but also instills a renewed sense of confidence among your ranks.
Your decision to send the cavalry to harass Ottoman forward formations takes a disastrous turn. The seemingly straightforward plan unravels as the Turks send their light steppe horsemen to intercept your force. They are more formidable than expected and manage to repel your cavalry. What was intended as a show of strength turns into a minor defeat as both sides suffer casualties.

choices.label: It is time for the Imperator to stretch his legs. I am going to personally lead the cavalry charge. Our goal is to kill as many of them as possible and retreat.
choices.text:

choices.text: Ashes and dust will be all that will greet our invaders. Let them feast on that! We must hope that they will not be able to procure enough food to sustain this siege for long...

choices.label: Infiltrate the Ottoman camp and recruit local informants. 5,000 gold; usually 1–2 agents.
choices.text: Quiet approaches to interpreters, drivers and camp followers establish {$openingAgents} new agents inside the Ottoman camp. Their reports will begin reaching your spymaster.

choices.label: The Severan Wall is the weakest of the three, but it protects the Great Palace and the heart of the city. It must be rebuilt. \[Materials -80\]

choices.label: [Focus - Fortifications and Artillery\] All the three Walls must be restored before the siege begins - the siege will be long and hard. \[Materials -250\] #focus:0

events.title: Siege Preparation — Call on a Major Christian Power

choices.label: Send our envoy to the Pope. As the leader of Christendom, he is guaranteed to provide at least some aid.
choices.text:
The Pope sends 6 ships packed with food, carrying money and 600 archers, along with his letter in which he offers his prayers for the soul of Constantinople and a promise of further aid.
The Pope sends 2 ships packed with food, carrying money and 200 archers, along with his letter in which he offers his prayers for the soul of Constantinople.

choices.label: [Focus - Diplomacy and Spycraft\] As we have accepted Catholicism fully, send our envoy to the Pope and request him to launch a new crusade to help us! #focus:4
choices.text:
Tireless work of your diplomats and the wise decision to mend the Schism create the conditions which allow the Pope to call the Xth crusade, this time to protect Constantinople and repay the sins of the IVth crusade, when Western crusaders sacked the City! Soon, pilgrim warriors flock to your cause, Italians, French, English, Scottish, Spanish, Germans, Portuguese, Hungarians, Polish, Lithuanians, Danes and even a few Swedes. Over the coming months some 3000 infantry, 4000 archers and 800 cavalry arrive, along with maybe 15 000 pilgrims and camp followers who join your general population. The morale of your defenders has never been higher!
While the Christian kingdoms are not yet ready to commit to a full crusade, many send their volunteers to help you. Venetian and Genoese mercenaries also soon arrive, bringing 600 infantry and 600 archers to support the defence of your city.
Memories of the defeat at Varna are too fresh... Your call for a new crusade falls on deaf ears, but you do receive a lot of supportive thoughts and prayers directed your way. Some even send you some money, but it feels like a disappointment...

choices.label: [Focus - Faith and Unity\] As we have embraced the truth of Orthodoxy and rejected Roman heresy, we send our envoys to Trebizond and the Georgian Kingdom, stressing that if Constantinople falls, it will be the end of the Orthodox world and that they will be next. Announce the first Orthodox Crusade to save Constantinople and call all righteous Stavrophoroi - Orthodox crusaders - to our banner! #focus:3
choices.text:
In our days, Orthodox realms are few and weak, but your call raises their hearts and triggers an unexpected movement of support for your cause. Orthodox monks from the villages of Ruthenia to the mountains of Armenia ring bells and preach the need to defend Constantinople. Soon, pilgrim warriors flock to your cause, Bulgarians, Georgians, Armenians, Serbs, Ruthenians and even a few Cossacks. Over the coming months some 8000 infantry, 2500 archers and 1200 cavalry arrive, along with maybe 15 000 pilgrims and camp followers who join your general population.
In our days, Orthodox realms are few and weak, and there is no will among them for a crusade, but some nonetheless answer the call. Georgian nobility sends 100 young knights and soon a ship of volunteers from Ruthenia arrives, adding another 400 infantry. Also 200 Armenian archers join your cause as well.
In our days, Orthodox realms are few and weak. They close their eyes and ears to your pleas.

choices.label: Make a general call for help to all the Christian realms. You know that your success here will depend greatly on how you managed to mend the Schism...
choices.text:
In our days, Orthodox realms are few and weak, but they answer the call. Georgian nobility sends 50 young knights and soon a ship of volunteers from Ruthenia arrives, adding another 200 infantry.
Your recent conversion to Catholicism has moved the hearts of believers. Knights Hospitaller have sent their fleet from Rhodes to support you, bringing 100 knights, 200 archers, 200 infantry and 5 ships.
While you are not enforcing Union of Florence, pragmatically minded Italians nonetheless see an opportunity to find a place for themselves in your new Empire. Venetian and Genoese mercenaries soon arrive, bringing 400 infantry and 400 archers to support the defence of your city.

choices.label: Infantry is the backbone of our army, they will hold the walls during the enemy assaults. Raise 3000 infantry.\[Cost - 30 000 gold\]
choices.text: We quickly recruit more spearmen from the citizens of Constantinople. Some have never held a weapon in their lives. They will learn quickly or they will die. \[Money -30000\] \[Infantry +3000\]

choices.label: Nothing is more dangerous when approaching the walls than a well-aimed arrow. Ranged troops are most effective at killing attackers - raise 1500 archers.\[Cost - 30 000 gold\]
choices.text: You order the ancient Hippodrome to be converted into three archery ranges, where hundreds of archers train daily. By the time the siege comes, they should be ready. \[Money -30000\] \[Archers +1500\]

choices.label: Cavalry allows us to sally out and strike at our enemy directly, but also the knights can dismount and fight on the walls, so let us raise 300 cavalry.\[Cost - 30 000 gold\]
choices.text: One does not become a knight overnight, but you hurry to ennoble promising candidates. This new force will train day and night to prepare for the war. \[Money -30000\] \[Cavalry +300\]

choices.label: [Focus - Mobilisation\] Return to tradition and raise a Legion of 5000 infantry and 1000 archers, in honour of our Roman ancestors. \[Cost - 50 000 gold\] #focus:1
choices.text: On your orders, the whole city is turned into a massive training encampment. As per ancient tradition, a legionary Aquila is forged from gold, perched atop an Orthodox Cross, joining the Roman heritage with our Christian faith. Freshly minted legionaries are motivated, but only time will tell if they deserve the name of their forebears. \[Money -50000\] \[Infantry +5000\] \[Archers +1000\] \[Troop Morale +10\]

choices.label: [Focus - Faith and Unity\] We call upon the religious fanatics, forming their mobs into military units. They will be poorly trained, but cheap to raise. \[Cost - 3000 gold\] #focus:3
choices.text:
While the nobles don't like our decision, these new fanatical troops are very motivated and numerous, numbering around 3000. But the best thing about them is that they are cheap - all we need to do is to pay for their weapons. However, they are not trained, don't like taking orders from your officers and the overall quality of your infantry suffers. \[Money -3000\] \[Infantry +3000\] \[Noble Support -5\] \[Troop Morale +30\] \[Infantry Quality is decreased\]

choices.text: The muster rolls are closed for now. No new troops are raised; the existing garrison will have to carry the burden.

choices.label: They should remain where they are and protect our lands from bandits and raiders, support of the nobility will be important to me.
choices.text: The nobles are pleased with your decision and promise to make good use of the imperial troops to protect your lands. They also send you a monetary contribution worth 15000 gold to support siege preparation. \[Money +15000\] \[Noble Support +5\]

choices.label: Summon all of the trained troops to return to Constantinople. If the City falls, nothing else will matter, we need every bow and every blade on our holy walls!
choices.text: Soon, a few ships from Morea arrive, bringing the whole garrison - a total of 1000 soldiers, 400 archers and 100 cavalry. The people of the City rejoice, as this significantly bolsters your forces. \[Infantry +1000\] \[Archers +400\] \[Cavalry +100\] \[Noble Support -10\]

choices.label: We have enough food and this siege won't take longer than a month - there is no need to waste money or worry people.

choices.label: Buy all the food in the city. \[Cost - 6000 gold\]

choices.label: Buy all the food in the province.\[Cost - 15 000 gold\]

choices.text: Desperate times call for desperate measures. We have spent so much money that our treasurer is crying, but at least our warehouses are absolutely brimming with food.

choices.text: With an iron fist Imperator has declared that food in your mouth now belongs to the Empire and you will eat only when you are ordered and only how much you are ordered. Everyone is unhappy, but everyone will have something to eat.

choices.label: Allow Galata to remain neutral, but use your Imperial privilege to demand that they provide us with troops, supplies and money for the siege.
choices.text: You demand troops, provisions and money under your imperial privileges. The podestà sends what he can, protesting that you are dragging Galata into the war. The supplies arrive; the warmth of his letters does not.

choices.label: Send gifts to the people of Galata and remind them of their duty to Christianity, asking them to join you. #focus:3
choices.text: You dispatch generous gifts to Galata, coupled with an impassioned plea reminding them of their Christian duty. Framing their involvement as a moral obligation to protect the faith from Ottoman dominance, you also hint at the fact that after Constantinople the next target for the ambitious Sultan will be Galata itself. While Genoese are men of coin first and faith second, your appeal does have some effect - you can expect more support from them now.

choices.label: Ask Giustiniani to take control of Galata. His loyalty falls by 10; decide his reward after capture. #focus:4
choices.text: You order Giustiniani to secure Galata. The territorial settlement remains yours to decide. A Genoese captain will meet less resistance from its citizens than your own guards would. He understands the bargain perfectly. So do the men who will have to honour it.

events.title: Siege Preparation — The Great Chain of the Golden Horn

choices.label: They are fools! Without the Chain, Golden Horn will be open to enemy fleet assaults and we could lose access to Galata! We must keep the Chain.
choices.text: Your decision to retain the Great Chain proves crucial. As enemy fleets attempt to navigate the Golden Horn, they will be met with the formidable obstacle to their plans. The Chain holds strong, safeguarding the harbour and preventing potential assaults and our strategic access to Galata is preserved.

choices.label: They are right, the Chain serves no purpose in modern times. Scrap it and sell the metal.
choices.text: Workers dismantle the Chain and sell the metal. The treasury receives the proceeds; the harbour entrance must now be defended by ships and shore batteries.

choices.label: We shall defend our harbour with our cannons, get rid of the Chain and use the metal to cast ammunition and cannons. However, it will cost 5000 gold.
choices.text: Foundry workers cut up the Chain and recast the metal into cannon and ammunition. The work consumes gold, but new guns can now cover the harbour.

choices.label: The Chain is absolutely massive… We could ask Orban to cast the greatest cannon in the world from its metal. (5,000 gold)
choices.text: Orban has the Chain dragged to the foundry. The furnaces burn through the night, and the mould is packed beneath a forest of wooden braces. At last the Grand Cannon emerges. The gunfounders cheer; the treasurer asks whether anyone has weighed how much powder it will need.

events.title: Siege Preparation — Orders for the Fleet

choices.label: The fleet should be used to raid Ottoman food shipping and disrupt their logistics
choices.text: Our fleet will now engage in raiding activities, interfering with Turkish supply routes, causing Ottoman food supplies to run out quicker than they would otherwise.

choices.label: The fleet should be ordered to raid Ottoman coastal villages and target valuable merchant ships, we could use their plunder to fund the siege.
choices.text: Your fleet will now engage in a guerrilla campaign against the soft underbelly of the Ottoman Empire, attacking unprotected villages and trade ships, seeking to cause chaos and plunder gold to bring it back to you.

choices.label: As Rumeli fortress is no longer a threat, our fleet should establish a lifeline to the Genoese colonies in Crimea and bring us grain.
choices.text: On your orders the fleet will travel to Genoese colonies in Crimea, we know that their markets are full of cheap grain - they will run the blockade and keep bringing supplies to the city.

choices.label: Order the fleet to remain in the Golden Horn, protecting the city and shooting their cannons at the attackers.

Order the fleet to engage the Ottoman fleet in direct battle and destroy them.
choices.text: Your fleet finds the Ottoman ships off Lesbos and forces them into battle. By nightfall, the surviving enemy vessels are fleeing. News of the victory reaches the City ahead of the returning captains.

choices.label: Appoint Giustiniani. Infantry lethality +15%.

events.title: Siege Preparation — Assault on the Straitcutter Fortress

Their mission is to start a fire and create confusion, creating an opening to open the gate and let in the rest of your forces. The mission goes flawlessly - the infiltrators skilfully navigate Ottoman defences and soon your troops raise your banner over the Boğazkesen. Your troops capture the enemy cannons which will be useful in the defence of our City and explode the gunpowder stores, turning the fortress into a ruin and opening the way to the Black Sea. \[Straits are Open\] \[Cannons +5\] \[Troop Morale +10\]

He is successful - the ammunition warehouse explodes with a thunderous roar, destroying the main artillery tower, destroying all the cannons and the ammunition required to fire it. The mission is a complete success and while Ottomans will eventually rebuild the castle, for now the Strait lies open once more. \[Straits are Open\]

You order a sabotage mission and your spies bribe a Levantine sentry to set the gunpowder storage on fire. Unfortunately, Ottoman guards keenly guard the armoury and detect the sabotage attempt. Despite best efforts, the mission fails and our saboteur is executed. The artillery remains operational, maintaining the blockade of the Strait. Fortunately, the only thing we lost is a bit of money. \[Money -3000\]

choices.label: Launch a sudden assault and take the castle at any cost. This will guarantee our victory, although at a great cost. \[High casualties\]
choices.text: You realise that taking this fortress is critical for the survival of your City. The sudden assault catches Rumeli’s defenders off guard, and the well-equipped contingent led by the seasoned commander overwhelms the defences. The fortress falls under your control, securing the Bosphorus Strait, but the price for this is great, as direct assault is always costly.

choices.label: Undermine the foundations - send your engineers to put explosives underneath the fortress \[Risk - Engineers & Ammunition\]

You deploy your engineers to dig tunnels beneath Rumeli Fortress, intending to collapse its walls by igniting explosive charges. Your engineers complete the tunnel and successfully detonate the charges, causing the fortress walls to collapse. The fortress is now barely more than a smoking ruin, leaving the Strait open.
You deploy your engineers to dig tunnels beneath Rumeli Fortress, intending to collapse its walls by igniting explosive charges. Unfortunately keen-eyed Ottoman scouts discover the tunnels and collapse them before your sappers reach their destination, trapping and killing your engineers. It is a black day, we will not have access to the Black Sea.

choices.label: Conserve our strength and do nothing, we do not need access to the Black Sea.
choices.text: Boğazkesen is too well fortified and we need all the men we can spare in Constantinople. However, this means that we will not have access to the Black Sea ports and their grain reserves.

choices.label: Have the scholars search the Blachernae archives for recipes and accounts of Greek Fire. \[Cost - 4000 gold\]
choices.text:
Scholars meticulously comb through the historical archives, unearthing fragments of information on Greek Fire. While the process is slow, their dedicated efforts yield valuable insights, providing a foundation for the rediscovery of the Greek Fire! We now have a powerful weapon in our hands against the Turks!
Scholars meticulously comb through the historical archives, trying to unearth fragments of information on Greek Fire. They discover many interesting secrets, but unfortunately the mystery of the Greek Fire appears to have been lost in the mists of time and cannot be found.

choices.label: [Focus - Faith and Unity\] Send an expedition to Mount Athos monasteries, where ancient manuscripts and forgotten wisdom are hidden. The monks most likely know the secret of the Greek Fire. #focus:3
choices.text: A daring expedition sets forth to the sacred Mount Athos, seeking the wisdom preserved by devout monks. The journey proves fruitful, as the monks, bound by faith and a sense of duty, share ancient manuscripts that hold the elusive formula for Greek Fire. We now have a powerful weapon in our hands against the Turks!

choices.label: Summon all the alchemists to test new methods to create Greek fire – invention beats rediscovery! \[Cost - 3000 gold\]
choices.text:
Through an unexpected stroke of genius, or perhaps sheer luck, the alchemists rediscover the ancient formula for Greek Fire. After months of trial and error, they successfully create a working version of the legendary weapon, one that burns fiercely and even floats on water. \[Technology Unlocked - Greek Fire\] \[Money -3000\]
While the alchemists cannot recreate Greek Fire, their experiments with explosive substances lead to an unexpected breakthrough - the creation of small, throwable devices that explode upon impact. These rudimentary hand grenades are not as destructive as Greek Fire but can be used as an effective weapon in close combat situations. We now have unlocked a new technology - Grenades! \[Technology Unlocked - Grenades\] \[Money -3000\]
Despite the best efforts of the alchemists, the process of recreating Greek Fire ends in failure. Their attempts at various combinations of chemicals and alchemical processes result in only smoke and minor explosions. Nothing close to the feared weapon is produced and your troops and nobles are disappointed. \[Noble Support -3\] \[Troop Morale -3\] \[Money -3000\]
The alchemists' reckless experiments take a disastrous turn. A chemical reaction goes horribly wrong, causing an explosion that destroys part of the palace. The explosion spreads fires across the lower levels, and several buildings are damaged - we will need to cover the costs of their reconstruction. \[Money -1000\] \[Money -3000\] \[Materials -25\]

choices.label: [Focus - Fortifications and Artillery\] We should not rely on legends for our defence. Battles of this modern age will be decided by steel and cannon, not some esoteric alchemy. (3,000 gold) #focus:0

choices.label: We have other matters to deal with, leave these fairytales for someone else.
choices.text: We decided that Greek Fire is not necessary for our plans on how to defend the City during the siege. Time will show if our decision was wise.

choices.text: Our parties evacuate stores and break minor crossings. Ottoman foragers stray into ambushes.

choices.text: Raiding parties strike the depots and wagons. Smoke follows the enemy’s advance, and displaced villagers crowd towards the City.

choices.text: The army will find ruined mills, empty granaries and contested roads. The soldiers call it preparation; the refugees have other names for it.

choices.text: Engineers identify the powder wagons and prepare timed charges. The explosion destroys guns that will never reach the walls.

choices.text: Your riders bring an imperial guarantee of pay and safe passage. The Serbian captain changes sides with five hundred men. The same men leave the Ottoman rolls and enter yours.

choices.text: The villages keep their stores and crossings. The Ottoman army will find its route unimpeded.

choices.text: Families pass through the gates under escort, carrying what the carts will bear. Some leave silently; others demand to know which oath they have broken. Orhan departs without a command. Their service is lost to us.

choices.text: The captains surrender their lists of men and weapons. Their soldiers are distributed among Roman companies, their movements watched. Orhan remains under guard. We have gained men, though few friends.

choices.label: Confirm their privileges and honour their service. Let Orhan command them. \[Infantry +300; noble support −5 points; Orhan available.\]
choices.text: You receive their oath before the court and confirm their households under imperial protection. Orhan kneels, then rises to receive his commission. Among the nobles, several faces remain carefully expressionless. On the muster ground, three hundred men answer the call.

choices.text: Diedo accepts the agreement. His ships enter your naval service, his volunteers join the garrison, and he becomes available as a commander.
