events.title: Food Riots in the Merchant Quarter

choices.label: Implement Price Controls for All Food Sales
choices.text: The Emperor decides to impose strict price controls on all food items, aiming to make them more accessible to the populace. This move prioritises affordability but may have consequences for merchants and the overall economy. Short-term relief is provided as prices stabilize, calming the riots. However, soon merchants will reduce their stocks, hiding them or seeking to sell them on the black market, exacerbating existing shortages and effectively reducing the amount of remaining food. The masses do not understand the cause and effect of your policy decisions and love you for your perceived wise decision. Meanwhile the nobility and merchants see the results of your actions and disapprove of them.

choices.label: Use Force to Disperse Rioters and Restore Order
choices.text: As a show of authority, the Emperor deploys city guard to forcefully disperse the rioters and restore order. This approach emphasises maintaining law and order but the people feel that the Emperor is taking the side of the rich merchants profiting from the siege. Immediate order is restored, but the use of force does not address underlying issues of food scarcity and high prices, causing anger among the people, although the merchants and the nobility are pleased that even during the siege city’s economy functions as normal.

choices.label: Hand Out Some Food to Appease the Masses
choices.text: To quell the unrest, the Emperor orders the distribution of limited food supplies among the rioters. This gesture is intended to provide immediate relief and demonstrate empathy for the citizens' plight. The distribution of food temporarily appeases the masses and eases tensions. However, this approach does not address the root causes of the food shortages.

choices.label: Order the most powerful merchants to form a food price cartel and control the rise of prices. (War Economy)
choices.text: The Emperor engages in negotiations with influential merchants to collaboratively control the rise of prices. This option seeks a cooperative approach between the ruling authority and the economic elite, potentially benefiting both parties. Prices are stabilized through a collaborative effort, providing a middle ground for merchants and citizens. This approach may lead to accusations of favouritism and deepen the divide between the powerful and the people, but we do not care, because the cartel is now easily taxable and will bring in additional taxes every turn.

choices.label: Use the storm as cover for a surprise assault — send out the cavalry. Lose 10 cavalry; inflict up to 100 casualties across enemy contingents
choices.text: Seeing an opportunity in the storm's cover, the Emperor orders a swift and surprise assault by sending out the cavalry to exploit the disorientation it may cause among the enemy forces. The surprise assault catches the enemy off guard, causing confusion and inflicting casualties. However, the storm also poses challenges for the cavalry, as many riders get lost in the storm and fail to return.

choices.label: Use the storm as cover for covert operations — send an agent into the enemy camp — +1 spies
choices.text: Recognising the storm's potential for concealment, the Emperor dispatches a skilled spy to infiltrate the enemy camp. The goal is to gather critical intelligence or disrupt enemy plans without direct confrontation. Under the cover of the storm the spy successfully infiltrates the enemy camp, he will now work there for your cause.

choices.label: Let the troops rest beneath the cover of the storm — +10 army morale points
choices.text: Acknowledging the toll of the prolonged siege on the troops, the Emperor opts to let them rest during the storm, providing an opportunity for recuperation and regaining strength, as there is little chance of any major attack by the enemy tonight. Troops appreciate the respite, and their overall morale improves.

choices.label: Deploy fire ships in the storm to confuse the enemy fleet — -1 ships; -2 enemy supply days
choices.text: Taking advantage of the storm's chaos, the Emperor orders the deployment of fire ships to confuse and disrupt the enemy fleet. The storm provides additional cover for the Byzantine naval forces to execute this manoeuvre. The fire ships create confusion among the enemy fleet, causing some vessels to scatter.

choices.label: Use the cover of the storm to scout out enemy positions and take prisoners — +1 secrets
choices.text: Recognising the storm's potential to obscure activities, the Emperor initiates a scouting operation, aiming to better understand the enemy positions and take prisoners. Soon your soldiers return with a few blindfolded captives, whom they squeeze until they have all the information about the current situation in the enemy camp. This increases our available intelligence.

events.title: Ottoman propaganda spreads within the City!

choices.label: Launch our own propaganda campaign!
choices.text: We order our own agents to spread counter-propaganda, emphasizing the enslavement for all citizens that awaits them if the City falls. Your rumours outline that the Sultan's terms were unacceptable, and that the Emperor acts in the best interest of the people. This scares the people slightly, but motivates our troops - they know that there is no way out but victory for them.

choices.label: Crack down on alehouses and inns to stop the rumours
choices.text: To stem the spread of rumours, we decide to implement a crackdown on alehouses and inns where the propaganda is gaining traction. This approach will suppress the dissemination of false information by targeting key locations. However, the population is still slightly displeased about the fact that their favourite places to relax and have a cup of wine are now closed and you lose some money.

choices.label: Order our spies to find and eliminate the source of these rumours (Diplomacy and Spycraft)
choices.text: Our spies quickly identify the people paid by the Ottomans to spread these defeatist rumours. Soon they end up at the bottom of the harbour with sacks of stones tied to their necks and all the rumours end.

choices.label: Request the priests to calm the people (Faith and Unity)
choices.text: At your request, priests address the rumours in their sermons and encourage people to avoid them like sin. While the rumours don’t completely disappear, the authority of the Mother Church and confident preaching minimise their effects.

choices.label: Ignore the rumours, may your actions speak louder than words
choices.text: Do not dignify the enemy's lies with a response. Focus on strengthening the city's defences and maintaining order.

choices.label: Execute the artilleryman responsible for the cannon which exploded
choices.text: This kind of negligence will not be tolerated! Incompetent gunner is stripped naked and his head is cut off in front of his whole detachment. Discipline will be maintained at all costs!

choices.label: It's only a bad dream... Since we hired Orban as our Master Gunner, his practices prevent all accidents.
choices.text: Hiring him was a valuable investment - our artillery force is possibly the most professional in Europe right now. Also, we receive news that Orban has managed to create some additional ammunition at no cost to us!

choices.label: This is war, accidents happen. Do nothing.
choices.text: The men feel unsafe around our cannons, morale drops.

choices.label: Let them pray for us
choices.text: This outpouring of faith will fortify the morale of our people, we welcome it!

choices.label: Join them in person, Emperor is with you!
choices.text: Your decision to join the crowds is greeted by loud cheers - people rejoice that the Emperor walks among them! However the priests don't like this decision as it turns a solemn vigil into a happy celebration.

choices.label: Use this opportunity to identify and grab more recruits for the military
choices.text:
As some young men have been evading their chance to serve the Emperor, gathering of crowds in the streets offers a fertile ground for your recruiting officers. While people will not be happy about this, additional recruits will defend our walls better than their prayers.
Seven hundred and fifty conscripts enter training. They will be ready in five days.

choices.label: Execute the thief, make him a lesson to others
choices.text: The thief is executed publicly, the harshness of the punishment intended to deter others from similar crimes - nobles and merchants strongly approve of enforcing law and order. While this decision enforces discipline and order, some people are not happy with your decision - they think that it's too harsh for mere food theft.

choices.label: Give him 10 lashes and a fine of 3 gold pieces.
choices.text: The punishment is seen as a balance between justice and mercy. While some citizens believe the thief got what he deserved, others question how a starving man is expected to pay such a fine. This response maintains law and order but may exacerbate underlying social tensions as people grapple with the perception of fairness.

choices.label: Let the poor man go, this won’t change anything.
choices.text: Releasing the thief without punishment may be interpreted as a gesture of compassion but also risks undermining the authority of the Emperor. Other desperate citizens might be emboldened to steal, thinking there are no severe consequences for such acts. Indeed, over the following weeks, more cases of food theft are reported across the city, but people think of you as a merciful ruler.

choices.label: Do what Jesus would do - invite the man to your table, dine and talk with him. (Faith and Unity)
choices.text: The Emperor personally engages with the thief, learning about the plight of the city’s most desperate. This act of magnanimity inspires loyalty and admiration among the populace. However the nobility are outraged by this act. Also, the thief does know a certain secret that he shares with you...

choices.label: Make use of this thief (Diplomacy and Spycraft)
choices.text: This thief appears to be a talented infiltrator - let us train him to become our spy.

choices.label: Well done, let's wait for the harvest.
choices.text:
If all goes well, eventually they will see the fruits of their labour.
The gardeners expect a first harvest in twenty-five days.

choices.label: This is a waste of time. Direct those people to collect materials for the wall repair instead.
choices.text: You order the people who were trying to plant vegetables to instead go and help with deconstruction of some old buildings. People are not pleased, but this is more important.

choices.label: Bribe him to sing us praises instead
choices.text: The poet accepts the bribe and begins crafting verses that extol the Emperor’s virtues, weaving tales of his leadership and wisdom. The public, however, grows suspicious of the sudden shift in tone, causing some to question his authenticity.

choices.label: Allow the freedom of expression – it costs nothing and remains one of the few joys for our citizens.
choices.text: You decide to demonstrate your magnanimity by tolerating criticism, allowing the poet to continue his recitations. Unfortunately your soldiers really like one of his lewd songs about the Emperor ordering a Turkish whore and instead getting a Wallachian donkey. Paradoxically your soldiers love you more because of it, but the priesthood and the nobles are furious.

choices.label: Throw him into the dungeon
choices.text: The poet is swiftly apprehended and imprisoned, sending a clear message that dissent will not be tolerated. While this silences the critical verses, it also dampens public morale, as citizens perceive the Emperor as overly harsh.

choices.label: Recruit him for the military (Mobilisation)
choices.text: If he wants to sing, let him sing on the walls about the Sultan's arse! You order the poet to be apprehended and enlisted in the military. The poet, reluctant at first, finds himself inspiring troops through rousing chants and battle songs.

choices.label: This is what true citizenship is - praise them!
choices.text: Praising their efforts publicly, you let the citizens continue their work independently, fostering a strong sense of pride and morale. While the repairs might not be as efficient as those overseen by professionals, their efforts have a noticeable impact.

choices.label: Send some engineers to direct them. (Fortifications and Artillery)
choices.text: A team of skilled engineers is sent to guide the citizens' efforts, ensuring their work strengthens the walls more effectively and efficiently. Under professional supervision, the repairs hold up better against future cannon fire, reinforcing critical defensive points.

choices.label: See if any of them are talented and if so - promote them. (Mobilisation)
choices.text: You soon notice that a few of the citizen's leading the informal effort to repair the walls clearly have some talent for engineering. While repairing the walls if important, there are other tasks you would like to use them for, so you promote them to full engineers. Unfortunately, it means that the ongoing attempt to repair the walls does not produce much utility.

choices.label: Reward the most industrious workers with rations.\[Cost - 50 Provisions\]
choices.text: Recognising the extraordinary efforts of key individuals, you distribute extra food to them as a reward. This gesture encourages others to contribute to communal defence efforts and improves the quality of labour.

choices.label: Let’s hope these rumours turn out to be true…
choices.text: You do not comment on the rumours.

events.title: Rumours that no one is coming

choices.label: Let’s hope these rumours turn out not to be true…
choices.text: You do not comment on the rumours.

choices.label: Launch a night attack to surprise the enemy and cause chaos in their camp. (50% success) — Success: -300 enemy irregulars, -20 infantry, army morale +3; failure: -100 infantry, morale -3
choices.text:
The attack catches the Ottomans off guard, causing confusion and heavy casualties in their camp. Morale in the city surges as the enemy struggles to recover.
Unfortunately our poor coordination in the dark leads to heavy losses. The Ottomans quickly regroup and retaliate, leaving your forces weakened and morale shaken.

choices.label: Send the cavalry out at dawn, with the sun behind us. (50% success) — Success: -250 enemy irregulars, -10 cavalry; failure: -50 cavalry
choices.text:
At sunrise, the cavalry charges from the gates, using the blinding light to confuse the enemy. This bold move inspires our troops and creates panic in the Ottoman ranks.
Unfortunately the Turk spies catch wind of our plan and anticipate the charge with a formation of spearmen hidden among their tents. The cavalry suffers devastating losses, leaving the city with fewer resources for future battles.

choices.label: Send Turkish defectors to sneak into their camp and kill the guards. (90% success) — Success: enemy food -3, irregulars -150; failure: army morale -5
choices.text:
Orhan's hand-picked Turkish defectors blend into the Ottoman camp, taking out key guards and sabotaging supplies before escaping. This is a great victory for us, sowing chaos and terror among our enemies.
Unfortunately Orhan's infiltrators are caught and executed - their screams wake the City in the morning as they are tortured to death in front of the Walls. Even worse, some among our own are whispering that maybe Orhan is only pretending to be on our side and he made our plan fail. While you know that this is nonsense and that Prince Orhan would be the first one to lose his head if Mehmed took the City, these rumours lower morale of the troops.

choices.label: Attack the area where our soldiers and the Turks have a truce. (75% success) — Success: enemy food -4, irregulars -250; failure: -10 infantry
choices.text:
In a spot where neither side usually attacks, we launch a surprise strike. The Turks are taken completely by surprise, allowing us to break through their lines, burn their food stores and inflict significant damage to their forces.
Unfortunately the Turk spies catch wind of our plan and anticipate the attack. We don't manage to achieve our goals, but neither do we suffer any serious casualties ourselves.

choices.label: Use hidden tunnels to send elite troops behind enemy lines. (90% success) — Success: enemy food -5, cannon -1; failure: -100 infantry. The tunnel is lost either way
choices.text:
Using secret passages, our best soldiers attack the Ottoman camp from the rear, targeting supplies, cannons and sleeping soldiers. This is a devastating attack, that significantly weakens our enemies. In the aftermath of the attack the tunnels collapse, so unfortunately we will not be able to use them again.
Unfortunately the Turk spies catch wind of our plan and anticipate the attack. The tunnels are discovered, and your elite troops are trapped and slaughtered, a serious loss for us. In the aftermath of the attack the tunnels collapse, so unfortunately we will not be able to use them again.

choices.label: This is too risky, we cannot afford soldiers for this plan, abort this plan!
choices.text: As instructed, our war council abandons the idea of attacking the enemy directly.

choices.label: Order Immediate Repairs \[Cost - 25 Materials\]
choices.text: You prioritise the allocation of resources and manpower to swiftly repair the damaged sections of the outer wall. While this addresses the immediate threat, it strains already limited resources.

choices.label: Ignore the warning \[Wall deteriorates\]
choices.text: These are mere surface cracks. Ignore them.

choices.label: Ask Johannes Grant, our chief architect, to look into this
choices.text: Johannes goes to inspect the wall in person. After carefully analysing the issue he is happy to announce that the cracks are merely cosmetic - only the outer brick layer seems to be affected, and the inner wall is as strong as ever, so we don't need to take any further action. While he is there, Johannes even improves the wall slightly.

choices.label: We are already aware of this problem (Fortifications and Artillery)
choices.text: Our focus on Fortification has allowed us to send additional engineers to inspect our walls. After carefully analysing the issue they happily announce that the cracks are merely cosmetic - only the outer brick layer seems to be affected, and the inner wall is as strong as ever, so we don't need to take any further action.

choices.label: Verify the evidence against the suspect and catch him in the act, we must avoid any possibility of falsely accusing an innocent
choices.text:
After a deeper investigation we find out that the servant appears to be visiting a brothel in secret. While it is a sin, he seems to be no traitor. We are lucky that we have not sentenced an innocent man to death.
After a deeper investigation we find out that the servant is indeed a traitor - he was pretending to go to a brothel, but in fact, he was sending messages to the Turks, informing them of our food situation and troop morale. As we have witnesses and a proper investigation has been conducted, the spy is brought forward, publicly tried and executed on the walls of the City. While betrayal is a horrible thing, you are glad to be rid of this traitor and that you know for sure that you don't have blood of innocents on your hands.
After a deeper investigation we find out that the servant is indeed a traitor - he was pretending to go to a brothel, but in fact, he was sending messages to the Turks, informing them of our food situation and troop morale. Unfortunately, the traitor notices our agents following him and escapes the next night after setting our food stores on fire. We manage to put out the fire, but many barrels of grain were burnt to cinders. This is an unfortunate turn of events, but at least the traitor is no longer reporting from our ranks.

choices.label: There's no time to waste, arrest the traitor and publicly execute him to deter others.
choices.text: The accused traitor is apprehended, shackled, and brought forth before you and your court. The atmosphere is thick with solemnity as the crowd gathers to witness the judgement. A hushed tension pervades the air, marking the gravity of the moment. With a voice that carries both authority and a sombre acknowledgment of duty, the pronouncement is made by the herald. The traitor shouts out that he is innocent and all of this is a mistake, but executioner's axe cuts his justifications short, together with his head. The people are concerned, both because of the betrayal and because of how quickly and without second thought you dealt with the suspected person. Some start to murmur - what if you were wrong? What if the person in question was actually innocent?

choices.label: Ask George Sphrantzes to make him disappear.
choices.text: We are not completely sure if he's really a traitor, but we don't have the luxury of investigating. George Sphrantzes is a man of many talents and while most know him as our foremost diplomat, he also moonlights as our spymaster. After receiving your request, he simply nods - where there is no man, there is no problem. The next time the suspected traitor goes for a walk, he simply never returns. Unfortunately you will also never know whether he was a real traitor or merely an unlucky servant, but that doesn't really matter. Sphrantzes also notes that he did find a cache of jewelry in the servants' quarters, most likely stolen from the palace nobles and he will not need them anyway, so they are added to our treasury.

choices.label: We could confront the suspected spy and offer him to work for us instead, promising him a better reward and harsher punishment if he would refuse. (Diplomacy and Spycraft)
choices.text: In the dimly lit chamber, the suspected spy is brought before you, the air heavy with tension and suspicion. As you confront the shadow lurking within your ranks, your offer is simple - great reward or even greater punishment. The spy for a moment considers trying to lie, but your unflinching tone forces him to drop this idea. The traitor drops to his knees and accepts your offer, begging for mercy and simultaneously promising his undying loyalty. While you have little trust for his words, you know that under close supervision of your other agents, this spy could be of great use to you. Now you have a double agent who will be very useful for your future schemes...

choices.label: Announce that the heir of the Doukas family had an unfortunate accident and declare public mourning,
choices.text: We need to allow the Doukas family to save face and prevent any rumours. Because of this, you choose to publicly acknowledge the noble's passing, holding a grand mourning ceremony to honour his memory. This option emphasises empathy and solidarity, offering the court and the citizens an opportunity to collectively grieve and find solace. The Doukas family is grateful for this interpretation of his death, as it saves them from dishonour and the noble can be buried together with the rest of his family line.

choices.label: Announce that noble was possessed and committed a mortal sin of killing himself. His assets will be confiscated by the Emperor and he will be denied Christian burial.
choices.text: You decide that telling the truth is the best course of action, however this means that you need to take all the official secular and religious measures to punish the sinner. People who committed the ultimate sin of killing themselves cannot be buried alongside other good Christians on hallowed ground, so his body is wrapped in rags and left in the catacombs beneath the City without any ceremony. While seizure of his assets is substantial enough to compensate our efforts, the rest of the nobility is shaken by this event. However the common people are less worried than they otherwise would be - it is clear to them, that its merely nobles being sinful, an unwelcome, but not an unusual occurrence.

choices.label: This is a private matter and the Emperor has more pressing issues.
choices.text: You decide to leave this matter unaddressed, allowing the people and the nobles to think what they may. While this choice emphasises maintaining the semblance of stability and shielding the court from having to deal with the problem directly, the rumours spread and the mood of both nobles and commoners alike sours.

choices.label: Ask George Sphrantzes how could this situation be used to our advantage.
choices.text: Our spymaster is quick on his feet and soon a new rumour goes through the palace - poor noble was assassinated by foul Turkish spies! George Sphrantzes launches an immediate investigation of your nobles and their servants - everyone is too worried about the mysterious Turkish assassin that the fact of suicide is soon swept under the rug. Finally, Sphrantzes announces that the assassin was caught while trying to poison Emperor's breakfast and unfortunately imperial kitchen stores had to be purged to avoid any other poisoned food. Noble families were invited to send some of their food as a sign of support for the Emperor, which both allows them to feel useful and slightly increases our stores of provisions.

choices.label: Thank the Lord, there’s one fewer of those damned cannons…
choices.text: We warn our own artillerists to be careful and avoid something like this.

choices.label: Prince Orhan urges you to use the opportunity and let him launch a swift raid with his Turkish lancers! — -150 enemy irregulars; -5 cavalry
choices.text: Prince Orhan's Turkish blood can be clearly seen to give him an edge of nomadic warlike insights, so you listen to him. Seizing the moment, you order a swift raid, capitalising on the enemy's confusion to inflict further damage and send out a small party of Turkish riders to cut down deafened and confused enemies. They strike swiftly and within minutes turn back, having reaped a bloody harvest, prince Orhan rides in front of the pack, waving a cut-off head of an Ottoman gunner.

choices.label: Hear the report. ({FleetReportPreview()})
choices.text: The account is entered into the naval ledger. The ships return to their assigned duties.

choices.label: Question him under guard.
choices.text: His account names a ship already lost. Your guards seize him before he can reach inside his cloak. His papers reveal an Ottoman contact.

choices.label: Receive him alone despite the warning. (The Emperor risks death.)
choices.text: The visitor strikes before you can summon the guards. His concealed blade pierces your chest.

choices.label: Dispatch Troops to quell the fires
choices.text: You decide to dispatch well-trained troops equipped with water-soaked blankets and rudimentary firefighting tools to respond to the fire in the Phanar district. Disciplined troops swiftly move to the forefront, forming an efficient line to combat the encroaching flames. The soldiers manage to contain the blaze effectively, preventing further devastation to residential areas and key structures, however the casualties are primarily concentrated among our troops and they resent being used like this.

choices.label: Enlist citizens for the bucket brigades
choices.text: As the call to action rings throughout the Phanar district, able-bodied citizens rally to form an impromptu human chain. Armed with buckets filled from available water sources, they combat the encroaching flames threatening their homes and community. The bucket brigade, composed of determined individuals from all walks of life, proves to be a formidable force against the fire. With each passing bucket, they create a continuous stream of water directed at the heart of the blaze. The citizens, working together with shared determination, manage to contain and extinguish smaller outbreaks, preventing the fire from spreading further. However, these people are not trained to deal with something like this and casualties among them are severe.

choices.label: Sacrifice the district and use demolition to stop the fires from spreading
choices.text: With a heavy heart, the decision is made to sacrifice certain sections of the Phanar district by implementing controlled demolitions. Your engineers, guided by a strategic plan, initiate precise demolitions to create firebreaks, effectively cutting off the path of the encroaching flames. As buildings crumble and controlled fires are set to consume predetermined areas, the sacrifice of these sections proves successful in halting the spread of the main inferno. The demolition strategy, while severe, prevents the fire from advancing further into other residential areas and critical infrastructure. Unfortunately among the sacrificed parts of the dockyard district were the warehouses and a lot of materials and provisions were destroyed in the fire. Your merchants are greatly displeased.

choices.label: Order the priests to pray in support of our firefighters
choices.text: A solemn decree is issued to the clergy, urging them to organise processions and prayers in support of the valiant firefighters. The streets reverberate with the echoes of religious chants as priests lead processions through the district, invoking divine intervention to aid those combating the encroaching flames. The collective prayers resonate through the air, creating an atmosphere of spiritual unity among the citizens and the courageous individuals battling the inferno. While the fires take a massive toll, the wind suddenly changes direction and fires seem to dissipate on their own. Was it divine intervention? It seems that all we suffer in the end is some minor damage.

choices.label: Alvise Diedo, our Venetian Admiral, rapidly reacts by deploying his sailors to fight the fires!
choices.text: Alvise Diedo, drawing on his experience as a captain, knows well that uncontrolled fire is nowhere more dangerous than on a ship or a dock, where one is trapped between the two elements. As soon as smoke appeared in the sky, Diedo acted without waiting for orders and quickly organised a firefighting response, successfully extinguishing the flames before they could spread further. Grateful merchants of Phanar repay him by gifting him a beautiful war horse, which he donates to your war treasury, claiming that he needs no reward, because what he did, any good Christian would do. On the other hand, it may also be due to reason that he feels himself much more comfortable on ship's deck than on a horse.

choices.label: Very unfortunate, but such is life.
choices.text: We shall remember his sacrifice.

choices.label: Send his family a small compensation.
choices.text: The engineer's family will receive compensation from you for his service. While it will not bring their husband and father back, it will help them to endure his loss more easily.

choices.label: This is merely a bad dream, Johannes Grant would not allow this...
choices.text: Johannes Grant is our siege commander and as an experienced architect he ensures that your ladders and scaffolding are always well maintained and no such stupid accidents occur.

choices.label: Have the cooks salvage what they can and serve it first. Risk a food-poisoning outbreak.
choices.text:
The cooks discard the worst grain and stretch the rest through the soup kitchens. No outbreak is reported, and the threatened stores are saved.
By morning, the infirmaries are crowded. A thousand civilians die; the garrison also loses men. You order the remaining spoiled grain burned.

choices.label: The poor will eat anything, order your cooks to sell the rotten food on the black market, somebody will buy it anyway.
choices.text: The grain finds buyers among those who cannot afford better. Your treasury receives 150 gold. Then reports of illness arrive from the poorer quarters: three thousand residents die in the outbreak. The palace kitchens and barracks remain untouched.

choices.label: Admiral Diedo, after he hears about your issue, suggests an alternative method.
choices.text: Diedo orders the stores sorted under his sailors' supervision. Sound grain is moved into dry barrels; spoiled sacks are destroyed. The careful inspection saves half the threatened stock.

choices.label: Burn the spoiled stores. Lose up to 150 provisions; remaining food stays safe.
choices.text: While it is unpleasant to throw away food while being under siege, it is better than having sickness inside the walls.

choices.label: Increase food rations - hungry soldiers are angry soldiers. — -50 provisions; +5 army morale points
choices.text: You decide to allocate additional provisions to the barracks to alleviate food shortages and ensure soldiers are adequately nourished for the challenges ahead. Boosting rations improves morale among soldiers, as it is always easier to concentrate on the defence of the city when your stomach is not growling.

choices.label: Relax the rules on whoring and drinking while on leave. — -24 infantry; -12 archers; -3 cavalry; +5 army morale points
choices.text: While normally military discipline needs to be quite strict in order to ensure that everyone is on their best behaviour, you realise that under current conditions, you need to motivate your men by relaxing these rules a bit. You announce that every seventh day some of the soldiers are allowed to leave their posts and go enjoy the drinks and whores, no questions asked, as long as they report back in the morning. While this policy quickly reduces tensions, unfortunately the rate of desertions increases, as some soldiers don't really want to return to the walls after tasting once more what freedom can offer...

choices.label: Organise more recreation and entertainment. — -500 gold; +4 army morale points
choices.text: You order your commanders to ensure adequate entertainment activities within the barracks to offer soldiers a much-needed respite from the rigours of military life. Soon, one of the detachments organises a drinking competition, while another one throws a comedy play. These activities improve morale and camaraderie among soldiers, serving as a valuable outlet for stress, although they cost some money.

choices.label: Ask Giovanni Giustiniani to intervene. — +6 army morale points
choices.text: The old condottiero over his life has spent more time with his soldiers than with his wife, so he knows them inside out. He goes straight to the barracks, has a stern talk with the Catholic mercenaries, then goes to the military chapel to pray with the Orthodox troops and finally goes and spends a night drinking with the detachment leaders. By morning all and any tensions among the troops are gone and everything is back to normal, at least for now.

choices.label: Ignore the issue. — -7 army morale points
choices.text: They are soldiers, they will get over it.

choices.label: Announce that help is approaching. Public morale +5; if the sighting is false, public morale later -8.
choices.text: The news passes through the markets faster than any ship could sail. For tonight, the City has something to look forward to.

choices.label: Wait quietly for confirmation.
choices.text: You tell the lookout to keep watching. Hope is precious enough without issuing it on credit.

choices.label: Share it with the sentries. Army morale +1.
choices.text:
The taste turns bitter. Your hand will no longer close around the cup. Someone shouts for a physician, but the poison has already done its work.
You break the loaf into portions. The sentries eat slowly, unwilling to finish it.

choices.label: Keep the loaf for yourself. Health +20.
choices.text:
Before the loaf is finished, your breath catches. The guards seize the baker as you collapse. There will be questions, but you will not hear the answers.
Warm bread, a little water, and a few minutes in which nobody asks for anything. You feel better than you have all morning.

choices.label: Return it to his family with thanks. Public morale +1.
choices.text: You ask him to carry your thanks home with the loaf. His family will dine better tonight.

choices.label: Ask the merchants' elders to arrange a fair queue. Merchant favour +1.
choices.text: The elders mark places with chalk and appoint a keeper. By noon, everyone is arguing about the chalk instead.

choices.label: Send the senior watchman to settle it. Army morale +1.
choices.text: The watchman separates the loudest disputants and makes them carry water for the oldest residents. His men approve of a problem with such an immediate solution.

choices.label: Resolve it personally. 70%: public morale +5. Failure: public morale -1, noble and clergy support -3.
choices.text:
You listen, establish turns and carry the first bucket to an elderly woman. The crowd cheers an Emperor who has come down from the palace to hear them.
Your compromise satisfies nobody. Someone asks whether you intend to negotiate with the Sultan as successfully. By evening, the palace and clergy have heard the remark.

choices.label: Ignore the quarrel.
choices.text: The argument continues without imperial assistance.

choices.label: Have a priest bless the post. Clergy support +1.
choices.text: The priest walks the parapet with a lamp and a prayer. That night, the watch seems less lonely.

choices.label: Let the men tell their story. Army morale +1.
choices.text: If their comrade still keeps watch, the soldiers say, the least they can do is keep him company.

choices.label: Faith and Unity: visit the post at night and pray.
choices.text:
In the stillness, a thought arrives with the force of a voice spoken beside you. Fragments of reports suddenly fit together. You cannot explain the certainty, but by dawn your agents have a useful lead.
You hear only the wind and the changing watch. Yet when you rise from prayer, the darkness seems less oppressive.

choices.label: Distribute it after watch. Army morale +2.
choices.text: Cups appear with impressive speed.

choices.label: Sell it. Gain 100 gold.
choices.text: A tavern keeper takes delivery before anyone can reconsider.

choices.label: Reserve it for the infirmary. Public morale +1.
choices.text: The barrel is set aside, still sealed, for the physicians.

choices.label: Pay for leather. Lose 100 gold; army morale +2.
choices.text: By evening, his apprentices are stitching beneath the shop awning.

choices.label: Ask wealthy households to contribute. Army morale +1; noble support -1.
choices.text: Saddles and spare leather arrive, accompanied by complaints about the frequency of imperial requests.

choices.label: Decline for now.
choices.text: The cobbler takes the ruined boot back to its owner.

choices.label: Display it in the guardroom. Army morale +1.
choices.text: The guards admire the strategic advantages of your proposed height.

choices.label: Send a small gift. Lose 25 gold; public morale +1.
choices.text: Your messenger returns with another drawing. This one includes a considerably larger crown.

choices.label: Issue emergency rations. Lose 100 provisions; public morale +1.
choices.text: Food is distributed through the neighbourhood. For once, the lamps are left to burn.

choices.label: Reprimand the household. Public morale -1.
choices.text: The missing candles are entered as theft. The hunger remains unentered.

choices.label: Accept his contribution publicly. Gain 25 gold; army morale +1.
choices.text: You take the purse before his comrades and thank him by name.

choices.label: Tell him to keep it. Army morale +2.
choices.text: "You have already given enough." He closes his hand around the purse and salutes.

choices.label: Allow a modest celebration. Lose 10 provisions; army morale +2.
choices.text: For an hour, the courtyard sounds like a place where people expect a future.

choices.label: Give permission without festivities. Public morale +1.
choices.text: They exchange their vows before he returns to the wall. Someone finds a flower for her hair.

choices.label: Release food from the public stores. Lose 250 provisions; public morale +2.
choices.text: Ration carts quiet the market more effectively than threats.

choices.label: Send guards to break up the fight. Public morale -1.
choices.text: The square is cleared. The price of onions remains a dangerous subject.

choices.label: Use the respite for repairs. Lose 10 materials; restore 1 point of current wall integrity.
choices.text: Masons work while the silence lasts.

choices.label: Let the men rest. Army morale +1.
choices.text: Men sleep against warm stone. The relief watch leaves them undisturbed.

choices.label: Let him perform it. Army morale +1; it may reach the Sultan.
choices.text:
The words travel across the lines. By afternoon, an Ottoman herald is demanding the offender's name. The Sultan has heard.
Laughter passes down the wall. For once, the enemy receives no explanation.

choices.label: Silence him. Army morale -2.
choices.text: The performance ends. The men return to their posts with noticeably less enthusiasm.

events.title: The Old Woman and the Stones

choices.label: Thank her before the workers. Public morale +1.
choices.text: You take one handle and help her carry it. Nobody cheers until the stones are safely down.

choices.label: Organise a working party around her. Lose 10 provisions; gain 10 materials.
choices.text: By noon there are twenty baskets moving through the street. She refuses a lighter one, but accepts someone to carry the other handle.

choices.label: Leave them to their debate.
choices.text: "Andrew was called first," Niketas insists. "And Constantine knew when to build a wall," says Leon. Their companions put another pot on.

choices.label: Join the debate.
Send materials to repair it. Lose 10 materials; public morale +1.
choices.text: The carpenters complain about the old beams, then set to work. By nightfall the bowls can return to the kitchen.

choices.label: Move the families into a noble residence. Public morale +1; noble support -1.
choices.text: A steward protests that the rooms were never intended for such numbers. You observe that the rain had made the same objection to their previous accommodation.

choices.label: Leave the repairs to the householders. Public morale -1.
choices.text: They stretch blankets beneath the rafters. The rain comes through more slowly.

choices.label: Send wine to the fire. Lose 50 gold; army morale +2.
choices.text: The cups pass between men who share few words. Someone begins a Greek song, and this time the foreigners listen.

choices.label: Stay and listen. Army morale +1.
choices.text: They make room on a bench. For the length of the song, you are another man far from an easier life.

choices.label: Accept the donation with public thanks. Gain 100 provisions.
choices.text: The carts are unloaded beneath the merchant's approving eye. His name is repeated often enough to satisfy a less ambitious man.

choices.label: Grant him a minor noble dignity and receive him personally. Gain 100 provisions; noble support +1.
choices.text:
As he kneels before you, his hand closes around something beneath his sleeve.
He bows so deeply that his chain strikes the floor. The older nobles welcome another household willing to pay for the City's survival.

choices.label: Assign an engineer for five days. Mentor and soldier temporarily unavailable; 80% chance of gaining an engineer when they return.
choices.text: The engineer takes the soldier aside before he can touch a powder measure. For five days they will work away from their regular posts. The first lesson is how to recognise what he does not yet know.

choices.label: Give him powder to practise alone. Spend 2 ammunition. 30% chance of gaining an engineer; otherwise he and 10 other infantry die.
choices.text:
Against the engineer's expectations, the young man proves a careful student. He earns a place with the gun crews and joins the engineer roster.
A flash runs into the loose powder. When the smoke clears, the would-be gunner and ten other soldiers are dead.

choices.label: Deny permission. He remains in the infantry.
choices.text: You tell him the wall still needs a man who knows which end of a spear to hold. The engineer opens his eyes again.

choices.label: Pay a boatman to investigate discreetly. Spend 50 gold.
choices.text:
He returns with mud on his sleeves and a scrap of sailcloth bearing a merchant's mark. Someone has been landing cargo where no cargo should be landed. The lights themselves remain unexplained.
He finds cold ashes, a length of wet cord and footprints ending at the water. He asks not to be sent again. You cannot tell whether he fears what he found or what he failed to find.

choices.label: Record the pattern and keep watching.
choices.text: Your clerk draws three dots in the margin. The following night there are no lights. Somehow this reassures nobody.

choices.label: Read the harbourmaster's report.
choices.text: {ReliefStormReport()}

choices.label: Account for the ships and the relief expeditions.
choices.text: {ReliefStormReport()}

choices.label: Close the inlet and repair the drain. Lose 20 materials; public morale +1.
choices.text: Workmen trace the leak and divert it. The water must be drawn elsewhere while the cistern is cleaned, but the neighbourhood accepts the inconvenience.

choices.label: Organise rationed water from another district. Lose 50 provisions to support the carriers.
choices.text: Carriers form a slow procession through the streets. The clean water arrives with complaints from the district supplying it. If the stores are short, they receive what remains.

choices.label: Keep drawing water and hope the filth settles. Risk an outbreak.
choices.text:
The keeper's reassurance proves worthless. One hundred residents die before the cistern is finally closed.
No great outbreak follows, but people carry their buckets farther rather than drink what you have declared acceptable.

choices.label: Pay labourers to remove it. Lose 50 gold; public morale +1.
choices.text: Ropes, a cart and several inventive curses clear the street before evening.

choices.label: Have the watch clear the alley. Army morale -1.
choices.text: The soldiers discover a use for their strength which none of them discussed with the recruiting officer.

choices.label: Let the hungry butcher it. Gain 15 provisions; risk illness.
choices.text:
The meat fills bowls that were empty. Within days, twenty of those who ate it are dead.
The carcass disappears quickly. People ask few questions about the stew.

choices.label: Destroy the affected sacks. Lose up to 100 provisions.
choices.text: The contaminated stock is removed. The storekeeper starts inspecting the next row with considerably less confidence.

choices.label: Pay for sorting and pest control. Lose 75 gold and up to 25 provisions.
choices.text: Workers separate sound sacks from spoiled ones and seal the holes beneath the shelves. The cats are pleased with the new arrangements.

choices.label: Issue the flour anyway. Public morale -2; risk losing 30 residents.
choices.text:
Thirty residents die in the sickness that follows. The remaining flour is withdrawn too late for them.
There is no recorded outbreak, but the bakers have no intention of forgetting the order.

choices.label: Supply cloth and pay relief workers. Lose 100 gold; public morale +2.
choices.text: Fresh hands take the ropes. Names are recorded before the bodies leave, so that their families have somewhere to bring their grief.

choices.label: Ask the parishes for volunteers. Clergy support +1; army morale -1 as soldiers assist.
choices.text: The priest divides the work among volunteers and a few reluctant soldiers. The cart moves before sunset.

choices.label: Leave the burial party to manage. Public morale -3.
choices.text: The cart is still there when the church lamps are lit.

choices.label: Investigate the burial trade. Spend 100 gold; an inquiry follows in three days.
choices.text: Quiet questions begin among shroud sellers, porters and those who work after the church doors close.

choices.label: Pay for a guarded reburial. Lose 50 gold; public morale +1.
choices.text: The widow accepts your help. The man cutting grave-ropes remains unknown.

choices.label: Dismiss the petition. Public morale -2.
choices.text: She takes the rope away. It is shown to other people before the day is over.

choices.label: Fund discreet treatment. Lose 100 gold; army morale +1.
choices.text: The physician treats what he can. The men learn that reporting illness need not mean becoming the company's entertainment.

choices.label: Suspend leave and order medical inspection. Army morale -2.
choices.text: The order produces resentment, then a surprisingly long queue outside the infirmary.

choices.label: Ignore the complaints. Lose 5 infantry; army morale -1.
choices.text: Five men become too ill for duty and leave the fighting roster. Their complaints are harder to dismiss when they cannot climb the stairs.

choices.label: Require payment and punish threats. Public morale +2; army morale -1.
choices.text: Officers collect the debts. The offenders discover that carrying a weapon does not place every civilian account beneath them.

choices.label: Pay the debts from the treasury. Lose 100 gold; public morale +1.
choices.text: The keeper is paid. She asks whether she should send the next bill directly to the palace.

choices.label: Refuse to intervene. Public morale -3.
choices.text: She folds the list carefully. Other businesses begin closing when the soldiers come off watch.

events.title: A Woman at the Barracks Gate

choices.label: Hear her witnesses and investigate. Public morale +1; army morale -1. A report follows.
choices.text: A clerk records each account separately. Theodora gives dates and names without once asking what you think of her profession.

choices.label: Put her under civilian protection while local magistrates hear the case. Lose 50 gold.
choices.text: She receives safe lodgings and a hearing beyond the accused men's barracks. The investigation will take longer, but it can proceed.

choices.label: Protect the soldiers from inquiry. Public morale -4.
choices.text: "Then I know what your protection is worth," she says. The gate closes behind her.

choices.label: Return the room to the soldiers. Army morale +2; noble support -1.
choices.text: The trunks leave by the back stair. The captain salutes with the exact amount of enthusiasm regulations require.

choices.label: Pay for separate lodgings. Lose 100 gold; army morale +1.
choices.text: Everyone sleeps indoors. The treasury has subsidised a romance it was never consulted about.

choices.label: Overlook it. Army morale -3.
choices.text: The soldiers make room beneath the awning and remember who was entitled to comfort.

events.title: A Child Left at the Tavern

choices.label: Pay a household to provide care. Lose 50 gold; public morale +2.
choices.text: A woman with milk and space takes the basket. Your clerk records the arrangement so the payment does not vanish into somebody else's account.

choices.label: Ask the parish to arrange care. Clergy support +1.
choices.text: The priest finds a household willing to help. The argument about the father continues without its smallest participant.

choices.label: Leave the matter to the tavern keeper. Public morale -1.
choices.text: He moves the basket farther from the draught. Somebody has to.

choices.label: Replace the shortfall. Lose 250 gold; army morale +2.
choices.text: Good coin settles the immediate dispute. The treasury clerk is told to find out where the bad money entered the pay chest.

choices.label: Offer rations instead. Lose 100 provisions; army morale -1.
choices.text: They accept food they can weigh, though the captain makes clear that supper is not the same as wages.

choices.label: Refuse compensation. Army morale -4.
choices.text: The men take back the coins. Their arithmetic now includes the value of continuing to serve you.

choices.label: Follow the invoices. Spend 100 gold; investigate in three days.
choices.text: Your clerk keeps the sack, the seal and the invoice. None can be explained away separately now.

choices.label: Accept replacement stock and close the matter. Gain 50 provisions.
choices.text: The replacement grain is inspected carefully. The false signature remains unexplained.

choices.label: Confiscate the dealer's remaining stock. Gain 100 provisions; merchant favour -5.
choices.text: Other merchants complain about punishment without inquiry. The dealer says very little.

choices.label: Ask the envoy's attendant to examine the clothing. Spend 50 gold on a protected inspection.
choices.text:
The attendant recognises a cheap imitation of the household badge. You can expose the deception without pretending to know who the dead man was.
He identifies the envoy's clasp, but cannot swear to the face. You announce the evidence honestly and order prayers for the missing man.

choices.label: Honour the dead without accepting the enemy's claim. Clergy support +1.
choices.text: A priest prays from the wall for a man whose name is unknown. The garrison receives an answer more dignified than the spectacle below.

choices.label: Forbid discussion of the display. Army morale -2.
choices.text: The men lower their voices. They do not stop looking.

choices.label: Send a guarded rescue party. Risk 10 infantry; possible rescue of 40 residents.
choices.text:
Forty fugitives are brought inside, some supporting the wounded. The officer keeps his party together until the last gate-bar is down.
The cries draw the rescuers into an ambush. Ten men do not return. At dawn the enemy has removed both bodies and evidence.

choices.label: Answer from the wall and lower a rope only where the guards can see. Gain 5 residents.
choices.text: Five people reach the rope. Others disappear into the darkness before your men can find a safe way to help them.

choices.label: Keep the gate closed and order silence. Public morale -2.
choices.text: The voices eventually stop. Nobody asks the officer whether that is good news.

choices.label: Search the city before passing judgment. Spend 50 gold; inquiry follows.
choices.text: The search begins with pay clerks and taverns, rather than a list of punishments.

choices.label: Offer an amnesty for immediate return. Recover 6 infantry; army morale -1.
choices.text: Six men return before dawn. The others have gone beyond the reach of the proclamation.

choices.label: Declare them deserters. Army morale -2.
choices.text: Their names are struck from the rolls. The sergeant has his answer; the City still lacks twelve defenders.

choices.label: Hold an open hearing for complaints. Public morale +2; noble support -1; reduce his influence.
choices.text: You hear petitions without promising to grant every one. Gennadius calls the gesture theatrical, but some of his listeners have already joined your queue.

choices.label: Faith and Unity: answer that authority also stands under judgment. Clergy support +1; reduce his influence.
choices.text: Your reply distinguishes authority from innocence. Several priests repeat it, depriving Gennadius of the claim that the palace has no answer.

choices.label: Ignore the sermon. Public morale -1; his following grows.
choices.text: The palace offers no reply. His listeners supply their own explanation.

choices.label: Wonderful, harvest everything and carefully ration the food.
choices.text: The harvest goes into the public stores. Fresh food and the promise of further crops lift spirits across the City.

choices.label: Let the people enjoy the fruits of their labour, they deserve it.
choices.text: Most of the food is either immediately eaten or sold on the black market, but the people are happy.

choices.label: Sell the harvest to merchants. Gain 1,500 gold; public morale falls by 8 points.
choices.text: Your soldiers turn up during the harvest and confiscate all of the vegetables. People try to protest, but are quickly silenced and told that this is for the good of the City. By your order the harvest is sold to rich merchants and your treasury gets a quick influx of cash.

events.title: The Shroud with the Blue Stitch

choices.label: Follow the payments to their buyer. Spend 50 gold; continue the inquiry.
choices.text: Marked coins pass through the dealer's hands. Your men wait to see where they go next.

choices.label: Punish the thieves and restore what can be identified. Public morale +2; clergy support -1.
choices.text: The sexton's public disgrace angers his protectors, but the stolen linen goes back to the families.

choices.label: Stop the inquiry quietly. Public morale -1.
choices.text: The dealer closes his stall for a few days. Nobody mistakes this for a conviction.

choices.label: Seize the profits and appoint a replacement. Gain 300 gold; noble support -3; public morale +2.
choices.text: The wards remain open. Only the signatures on the invoices change, to the disappointment of those who expected indispensability to protect them.

choices.label: Keep the evidence as leverage. Gain 1 secret; public morale -1.
choices.text: The official now answers your letters promptly. The widow never learns why the inquiry ended.

choices.label: Order restitution without a public trial. Public morale +1.
choices.text: Families receive payment and the contractor loses his position. The arrangement leaves fewer enemies and fewer answers.

choices.label: Offer a paid intelligence position and protection. Spend 1,000 gold; gain 1 agent.
choices.text: You arrange payment, a handler and a safe means of contact. She accepts the work after asking questions your intelligence officers should have anticipated.

choices.label: Ask her to give a statement about the visitor. Gain 1 secret; she remains a civilian.
choices.text: Her description includes a ring, a shipping mark and a habit of mispronouncing a Greek street name. It is enough to begin an inquiry.

choices.label: Thank her and leave her in peace. Public morale +1.
choices.text: The case is finished. For once, protection from the Emperor has required nothing further in return.

choices.label: Protect the porter and inspect the ledgers. Spend 100 gold; continue the investigation.
choices.text: The porter is moved to safe lodgings. His directions lead to a second set of books hidden beneath an ordinary floorboard.

choices.label: Raid the warehouse immediately. Gain 150 provisions; merchant favour -5.
choices.text: You recover sound grain. By the time the clerks arrive, the more interesting papers are ash.

choices.label: Close the investigation. Public morale -1.
choices.text: The porter disappears into another district. The warehouse changes its sign.

choices.label: Prosecute the ring and recover the stock. Gain 300 provisions; noble support -3; public morale +3.
choices.text: The purchasing official's relatives protest. Honest traders quietly bring your clerks further evidence.

choices.label: Demand restitution and continuing supplies. Gain 500 gold and 100 provisions; merchant favour -5.
choices.text: The ring buys its survival on terms favourable to the treasury. Whether anyone has learned honesty is another question.

choices.label: Keep the ledger as political leverage. Gain 2 secrets; public morale -2.
choices.text: The accused remain useful and frightened. The bakers receive no explanation for the inquiry's sudden end.

events.title: The Tavern with the Shuttered Door

choices.label: Recover the eight and pursue the boatman's connection. Gain 8 infantry; continue in three days.
choices.text: The eight return under your protection. Your investigators follow the boatman's promises towards the harbour.

choices.label: Pay the eight and end the inquiry. Spend 150 gold; gain 8 infantry and 2 army morale.
choices.text: They take their places on the wall. The paymaster learns that somebody else will cover his debts.

choices.label: Arrest everyone involved and close the case. Army morale -3.
choices.text: The cells fill, the watch remains short, and the boatman hears that questions have stopped.

choices.label: Return the men and expose the paymaster. Gain 4 infantry; army morale +3; noble support -2.
choices.text: All twelve missing soldiers have been accounted for. The paymaster's family discovers an urgent interest in procedural mercy.

choices.label: Return the men and use the crossing list. Gain 4 infantry and 1 secret.
choices.text: Your spies inherit the boatman's appointments. The four men return knowing exactly what passage would have cost them.

choices.label: Imprison the four and seize the passage money. Gain 200 gold; army morale -2.
choices.text: The treasury gains their fares. Their comrades see that returning alive has not necessarily improved their position.

choices.label: Fund an independent audit and relief. Spend 150 gold; public morale +2; reduce his influence.
choices.text: The audit does not make the City rich, but it puts names beside missing money. Gennadius finds it harder to claim that nobody will examine the accounts.

choices.label: Defend the war treasury without offering an audit. Noble support +1; public morale -1.
choices.text: You explain what the walls cost. He answers that an expense can be necessary and still conceal a thief.

choices.label: Ignore the sermon. Public morale -1; his following grows.
choices.text: The palace offers no reply. His listeners supply their own explanation.

choices.label: Order an inquiry into coercion and misuse of office. Public morale +2; noble support -2; reduce his influence.
choices.text: You distinguish private conduct from abuse of power and investigate the latter. Courtiers resent the questions; several households welcome them.

choices.label: Demand evidence for accusations against named people. Clergy support -1; reduce his influence slightly.
choices.text: The court asks for testimony rather than innuendo. Gennadius says a ruler should fear sin more than slander, but some listeners begin asking whom he actually means.

choices.label: Ignore the sermon. Public morale -1; his following grows.
choices.text: The palace offers no reply. His listeners supply their own explanation.

choices.label: Review recent favours and publish the reasons for appointments. Public morale +2; noble support -2; reduce his influence.
choices.text: Some appointments withstand scrutiny better than others. The review creates enemies, but it also gives disappointed men an answer more substantial than silence.

choices.label: Faith and Unity: challenge him to condemn envy in his own following. Clergy support +1; reduce his influence.
choices.text: You ask whether righteous anger excuses coveting a neighbour's office. The question divides his audience without denying its grievances.

choices.label: Ignore the sermon. Public morale -1; his following grows.
choices.text: The palace offers no reply. His listeners supply their own explanation.

choices.label: Distribute food and reduce court hospitality. Spend 200 provisions; public morale +3; reduce his influence.
choices.text: Food carts leave the palace under public supervision. Gennadius says charity extracted by shame is still charity. Some families care less about the motive than the bread.

choices.label: Open the palace accounts and explain rationing. Public morale -1; reduce his influence slightly.
choices.text: The figures reveal how little a cancelled feast would feed the City. They do not make hunger easier to bear.

choices.label: Ignore the sermon. Public morale -1; his following grows.
choices.text: The palace offers no reply. His listeners supply their own explanation.

choices.label: Meet a small delegation without armed ceremony. Public morale +2; reduce his influence.
choices.text: The delegates must turn slogans into demands. Some prove reasonable; others contradict one another. Gennadius can no longer speak for all of them without disagreement.

choices.label: Arrest Gennadius for obstructing the defence. Clergy support -10; public morale -3. Ends the sermon chain.
choices.text: The guards take him through a silent crowd. The streets clear, but his supporters acquire a story that imprisonment will not easily erase.

choices.label: Ignore the sermon. Public morale -1; his following grows.
choices.text: The palace offers no reply. His listeners supply their own explanation.

choices.label: Commit to a funded programme of repairs and hearings. Spend 200 gold; public morale +2; sharply reduce his influence.
choices.text: You name officials, allocate money and set dates. The promises can be checked. Several parish leaders agree to oversee the work.

choices.label: Invite parish elders to supervise existing relief without new spending. Noble support -2; reduce his influence.
choices.text: The palace yields some control to men who will have to answer to their neighbours. Gennadius must decide whether to welcome the arrangement or reveal how much he needs a quarrel.

choices.label: Ignore the sermon. Public morale -1; his following grows.
choices.text:
The palace offers no reply. His listeners supply their own explanation.
His following leaves the church in an angry procession. Shops close and officers report bitter exchanges at the posts. Public morale -8; clergy support -5.
The parish elders publicly acknowledge the changes. Gennadius still has critics to offer, but no united movement behind him. Public morale +3.
The movement remains an uneasy pressure upon the palace, but the feared confrontation does not materialise.

choices.label: Return to the day's business.
choices.text: The lookout resumes his watch.

choices.label: Accept the cargo and reward his courage. Lose 100 gold; gain 500 provisions. The ship departs.
choices.text: The captain receives your reward with a bow. His men unload the grain, then prepare to sail while the passage remains open.

choices.label: Accept his gift with thanks. Gain 500 provisions; the merchant keeps his ship.
choices.text: You cannot offer coin, but you thank him before the harbour workers. The grain enters the stores; the vessel remains his.

choices.label: Confiscate the cargo and ship for the defence. Gain 500 provisions and 1 ship; merchant favour -15.
choices.text: Guards take possession of the vessel. The captain's protests follow you up the quay. By evening, every merchant in the City has heard how an imperial welcome is repaid.

choices.label: Hire the company and its ship. Lose 1,000 gold; gain 30 infantry, 30 archers and 1 ship.
choices.text: The captain counts the coin twice. His men shoulder their equipment and follow your officers towards the walls.

choices.label: Decline. Let them sail away.
choices.text: The captain wishes you good fortune with the solemnity of a man who has decided not to share it.

choices.label: Admit them and take the vessel into service. Gain 200 residents and 1 ship.
choices.text: The passengers come ashore in silence until someone begins to weep. Harbour crews take charge of the empty vessel.

choices.label: Turn them away. Public morale -7; army, noble and clergy support -2 each; merchant favour -2.
choices.text: The vessel turns back towards open water. The crowd on the quay watches until it is too far away to hear.

choices.label: Pay him 250 gold.
choices.text: He counts the money and declares the misunderstanding resolved.

choices.label: Return the sealed barrel from the infirmary. Merchant favour +1.
choices.text: The merchant inspects the seal, bows, and has his porters remove the barrel. He leaves speaking well of imperial justice.

choices.label: Refuse compensation. Public morale -4.
choices.text: By evening, he has told half the market that the Emperor steals wine and the other half that he refuses to pay his debts.

choices.label: Sound the alarm and hold the parapet. Fight the assault with the current garrison.
choices.text: Bells ring along the wall. The attack will be resolved with your garrison's actual strength and defences.

choices.label: Rally the defenders personally. Lose 10 health; army morale +3 before the assault.
choices.text: You reach the stair at a run. Men who were hesitating follow you towards the fighting.

choices.label: Issue reserve ammunition. Lose 5 ammunition; army morale +2 before the assault.
choices.text: Fresh bundles reach the archers as the first ladders strike stone.

choices.label: Saints intercede; they do not compete for command. Let us ask both to pray for us. Clergy support +1.
choices.text: Niketas considers this. Leon nods as though it was what he meant all along. For a moment, the two men are satisfied.

choices.label: An emperor's judgment should settle the matter. Noble support +1; public morale -1.
choices.text: They defer immediately. The silence is impeccable and distinctly less friendly.

choices.label: Ask what troubles them beneath the argument.
Prayer is no bargain that purchases safety. We can honour your brother by protecting those still living. Public morale +2; clergy support +1.
choices.text: Niketas looks towards the crowded roofs. "Then I had better return to my watch." Leon goes with him.

choices.label: Promise that sufficient faith will guarantee victory. Army morale +2; clergy support -2.
choices.text: Some men cheer. The priest listening by the stair does not. You have made a promise that neither saint put in your mouth.

choices.label: Admit that you do not know, and pray with them. Public morale +1.
choices.text: The three of you stand together until the bell marks the changing watch. Nobody has won the argument.

choices.label: Draw and fight. Your fencing skill is {Fencing()}; skill improves defence and reduces injuries.
choices.text:
You turn his blade, force his arm aside and strike. The guards reach you as he falls. You lose {AssassinDamage()} health.
His first cut gets through. You stumble against the table before the guards drag him down. You lose {AssassinDamage()} health.

choices.label: Throw furniture between you and call the guards. Lose 10–25 health in the struggle.
choices.text: The table buys a heartbeat. His blade finds you as the guards seize his arms. You lose {AssassinDamage()} health.

choices.label: Thank the instructor and return them to duty.
choices.text: The engineer asks that the next volunteer be sent to him before being given powder.

choices.label: Purchase three days of emergency grain. ({EmergencyGrainCost()} gold)
choices.text: Grain carts arrive under guard. The storekeeper weighs the sacks himself. The City has enough food for the next three days.

choices.label: Requisition two days of food from noble households. (Noble support −5 points.)
choices.text: Your guards open private granaries and carry the sacks to the public stores. The owners write down everything taken. They will remember the Emperor's need when you next ask for their help.

choices.label: Give the garrison's reserve ration to the people. (One day of food; army morale −5, public morale +2 points.)
choices.text: The reserve wagons turn away from the barracks and towards the bakeries. Civilians receive bread. The soldiers hear where it came from before evening.

choices.label: Endure another day while we seek supplies. (Public morale −3, army morale −2 points.)
choices.text: The storekeeper closes the ledger. You send him to look again. Tonight the household eats quietly; beyond its doors, the City grows louder.

choices.label: Accept imperial control. Galata becomes an Ottoman military target.
choices.text: The imperial banner rises beside Galata’s own. The podesta remains administrator; this voluntary accession does not replay the capture-governance event.

choices.label: Preserve their neutrality; receive one diplomatic claim instead.
choices.text: Their friendship remains a diplomatic asset.

choices.label: Accept the diversion. Ottoman land operations delayed 2 days.
choices.text: The distraction buys two days.

choices.label: Keep the contacts in reserve. Gain one diplomatic claim.
