choices.label: Send 75 Varangians to arrest the conspirators. Lose 25 guards; Giovanni is imprisoned and Galata returns to imperial control.
choices.text: The guard breaks the conspiracy.

choices.label: Without the means to resist, concede the throne.
choices.text: You are deposed. Your reign ends; Giovanni’s seizure of the throne does not promise that the City will survive.

choices.label: Receive her into the household under guard.
choices.text: She is given a room beside the servants' court. Visitors and letters must pass through the chamberlain. That evening she begins a story about a king who made every guest surrender their shoes. Nobody slept better for it.

choices.label: Give her freedom and a place as a guest in the palace.
choices.text: Your secretary writes a deed of freedom. Shaherezade asks him to read it twice, then folds it into the cover of her book. ‘May I keep this even if you change your mind?’ The chamberlain assigns her a room in the outer household.

choices.label: Send her back with the envoy.
choices.text: She closes her book. ‘What shall I tell him?’ You tell her that the Emperor already has enough people to protect. She leaves with the envoy before sunset.

choices.label: Have your agents trace the letter and examine the book. (1 secret)
choices.text: Your agents copy the handwriting and follow the servant who carried the scrap. The book returns to its shelf with its stitches carefully replaced. Someone in the palace will discover that the Emperor can keep a secret too.

choices.label: Ask her to tell you the story in private. (Unsupervised access; risk of an attack.)
choices.text: ‘It is about a prisoner who taught a bird to carry water,’ she says. ‘The jailer mistook the bird for an omen. Everything that followed came from that mistake.’ You arrange an evening audience. The chamberlain's guards will wait outside.

choices.label: Keep her under guard and change the cupbearers' routine.
choices.text: The evening wine arrives at a different hour, carried by a different servant. Shaherezade remains in the outer household. From her room comes the scratch of a pen, stopping whenever a guard passes.

choices.label: Send her away before this goes further.
choices.text: She asks for her book and the clothes in her room. The chamberlain supplies an escort to the Ottoman lines. Neither the letter's author nor its intended recipient is found.

choices.label: Keep her alive in custody. Have the agents question her.
choices.text: The chamberlain takes her away. Her book remains on your desk, open at a story whose final page has been cut out. She will have time to explain who removed it.

choices.label: Offer protection in exchange for her contact and continued false reports. (+2 secrets)
choices.text: ‘He expects a message in my hand,’ she says. You give her paper. The first letter reports a fever. The second asks for instructions. Your agents collect the reply, and Shaherezade earns another evening alive. Secrets +2.

choices.label: Send her back, carrying the empty vial.
choices.text:
You send no letter. The envoy understands the message when he sees what she carries. At the gate she turns once, as though trying to remember the City from this side of the walls.
The Story's Missing Page: The cupbearer's assistant is caught copying your movements for an Ottoman courier. He admits planting the scrap among Shaherezade's belongings. The sewn pages in her book contain names and places: people she has been trying to find since her household was broken up.
Shaherezade listens while the chamberlain explains. ‘May I have my book back?’ she asks. ‘There are people in it I haven’t found yet.’

choices.label: Restore her book and offer her a free place as the court storyteller. (+1 secret)
choices.text: She accepts a room, a stipend and the right to leave. In the evenings she reads to the household. One story includes a gatekeeper's name your agents have been trying to learn. When asked how she knows it, she smiles. ‘Servants listen while important men are speaking.’ Secrets +1.

choices.label: Keep her under guard while the remaining letters are examined.
choices.text: She receives her book, but her door remains watched. The household has heard that she was cleared. It will also remember that she was kept a prisoner afterwards.

choices.label: Give her safe passage and let her leave.
choices.text: The chamberlain returns her possessions and obtains an escort. Before leaving she places one loose page on your desk: the ending of the story about the bird. The prisoner survives. The jailer never understands why.

choices.label: A. Invite her to your private apartments. Noble support -5; clergy support -10. Begins a personal intrigue.
choices.text: You dismiss the attendants. By dawn, Helena knows which imperial door sticks in its frame, and the servants know considerably more than they should. For once, the council's whispers concern something other than the walls.

choices.label: B. Ignore her advances. No immediate effect.
choices.text: You return to your papers. Helena studies the dispatches, then your expression. "How fortunate for the dispatches." She takes the wine with her.

choices.label: C. Arrange a marriage with {LadyMatchName()}. His loyalty +15; noble support -5. Begins a marriage intrigue.
choices.text: You offer Helena an imperial dowry in prestige rather than coin, and a place beside {LadyMatchName()}. Both accept. He sees an honour; she sees a household of her own. The families passed over for the match discover an urgent concern for proper breeding.

choices.label: D. Diplomacy: cultivate her as a source of secrets. Gain 1 secret; noble support -3.
choices.text: "Keep your admirers," you tell her. "Remember what they say." Helena laughs and names an official whose night-time boasting contradicts his accounts. By the following council, several nobles have noticed how closely you listen when she speaks.

choices.label: E. Diplomacy: recruit her as an agent. Gain 1 agent; clergy support -5.
choices.text: You give her a handler, a cipher and the means to report safely. Helena accepts on one condition: she chooses whom to approach. Her new errands attract clerical suspicion, but the intelligence office acquires someone who can enter rooms its sober gentlemen never see.

choices.label: Pay for its discreet recovery. Lose 1,000 gold; noble support -2.
choices.text: The letter returns with a faint smell of another man's perfume. You burn it yourself. The chamberlain leaves richer; discretion, it seems, is a taxable commodity.

choices.label: Acknowledge the affair and refuse to be blackmailed. Noble support -5; clergy support -10.
choices.text: Your refusal deprives the blackmailer of his price, though not the court of its entertainment. Helena takes your arm in public. The Patriarch requests a private audience of a rather different kind.

choices.label: Diplomacy: let Helena trace the blackmailer. Gain 1 secret; noble support -5.
choices.text: She sends a second letter, more enticing and entirely false. The man who comes to buy it supplies a name. You gain a useful secret, although the first letter remains beyond your control.

choices.label: Publicly defend the marriage and rebuke the gossip. Husband's loyalty +10 if still in service; noble support -5.
choices.text: You remind the court that a marriage under your protection is no invitation to a public spectacle. Helena thanks you without lowering her eyes. Several nobles resent the lecture more than they regret the gossip.

choices.label: Leave the couple to settle it privately. Husband's loyalty -10 if still in service; no faction reputation change.
choices.text: The palace doors remain closed. Your silence saves an argument at council, but an imperial promise of protection has proved disappointingly quiet when tested.

choices.label: Diplomacy: have Helena expose the slanderer's affairs. Gain 1 secret; husband's loyalty +5 if still in service; clergy support -5.
choices.text: Helena produces names, dates and a ribbon its owner would dearly like returned. Her tormentor falls silent. The clergy deplore a court which answers scandal by publishing a better scandal.

choices.label: Refuse publicly: +5 troop morale points, +10 Sultan fury points.
choices.text: Your refusal is read aloud at the gates. Your soldiers take heart; the envoy leaves in anger.

choices.label: Receive him courteously and question him before declining: gain 1 secret.
choices.text: Your household prolongs the audience and compares the envoy's claims with the reports of your scouts. You gain a useful piece of intelligence without making a promise of surrender.

choices.label: Execute the envoy. Sultan's fury +20 points; noble support −5 points.
choices.text: You order the envoy taken from the chamber. His letter remains unopened upon the table. By evening his riderless horse is sent through the gate; by dawn the Ottoman drums answer. Even those who praised your defiance find little to say of this.

events.title: Ottomans use prisoners to fill the Moat

choices.label: Order archers to fire on our enslaved people.
choices.text: Your command echoes across the walls, and reluctantly, your archers draw their bows. The first volleys rain down upon the enslaved prisoners, a brutal decision made in the face of strategic necessity. The moat is protected, but the atmosphere atop the walls turns dark. The morale of your troops falls, but you try to convince yourself that this sacrifice was necessary.

choices.label: We don’t need the moat. Fire only at the Turkish guards, but spare the labourers.
choices.text: You prioritise preserving the moral integrity of your defenders. The order is given to focus solely on the Ottoman forces, sparing the enslaved labourers. While the moat remains a formidable obstacle, your archers concentrate their fire on the advancing Turks. The labourers fill up the moat, but some of them use the opportunity to run over to the walls, your soldiers throw them down ropes and help them get over the walls.

choices.label: Open the gates: rescue 1,000–3,000 people, gain 5 troop morale points, lose 30 moat integrity points.
choices.text: The gates open under covering fire. Prisoners run towards the City while Ottoman archers shoot into the fleeing crowd. You bring survivors inside, but enemy labourers fill another stretch of the moat. Moat integrity -30 points.

choices.label: Emperor cannot abandon his people. Sally out!
choices.text:
The cavalry drives the guards away from the prisoners. The captives scatter towards the gates, and the Ottoman labourers abandon their work at the moat.

acceptedDecisions: Fixed 1452: January strategic focus; April A Fortress Rises on the Bosphorus; June Artillery Genius; December Union.
Eight flexible months in 1452 plus February 1453. Provisions and Galata are base selectable preparation events.
Hungry Mouths moves later, provisionally January 1453 alongside the Genoese arrival.
Career unlocks depend on the persistent number of game achievements, not achievements inside the current event chain. Required counts remain undecided.
Rumeli, Greek Fire and Overseas Grain Missions are career-unlocked preparation events. Every selectable event is titled Siege Preparation — ….
The diplomatic screen offers routine Galata interactions; the preparation event exclusively offers Varangian seizure and takeover through Giovanni.
Who Shall Govern Galata? fires only after successful capture by one of those routes, once per capture.
Galata has four states: neutral, direct imperial control, Giovanni autonomous, Turkish control. Appointing a governor alone does not grant autonomy.
Character loyalty to the emperor is a separate stat from troop morale, Galata goodwill and political control.
Castle sacrifice blocks Ottoman land operations for 5–9 days after siege begins; troop morale −5 points.
Giovanni can attempt a throne challenge after serious grievances and with sufficient political/military leverage.
One mission for the whole fleet; later changes cost an action; defeat leaves survivors; victory uses Victorious Fleet.
Galata preparation retains six core choices: support, neutrality, Varangians, bribe, Giovanni with Diplomacy focus, gifts/shared faith (+30 goodwill).
Post-victory Galata promise: +15 loyalty selected from +10/+15. Immediate autonomous grant: +30 loyalty and a positive defence bonus of undecided size.
Imperial and autonomous Giovanni Galata can be targeted by Ottoman land attacks during the siege, subject to the castle-induced action delay. Neutral or Turkish Galata cannot.
Chain, Fleet Orders and Commander are base selectable events. Successful commander appointment grants +10 army support once.
Naval Warfare is a newly authored base-event draft with five alternative investments. No fixed Galata treasury or troop inventory has been adopted.
